subject: polity
title: Constitution and constitutionalism
definition: A constitution is the fundamental law that sets up the organs of the State, distributes power among them and limits it; constitutionalism is the idea that governmental power must be exercised within those limits.
foundation_focus: Be able to define a constitution, list its functions and say where India sits on each classification axis.
mains_focus: Be able to argue why a written, mostly rigid-flexible hybrid constitution suits a diverse democracy, and the limits of constitutional supremacy.

subject: polity
title: Historical underpinnings: from the Regulating Act to the Government of India Act, 1935
definition: The sequence of British-era enactments and reforms whose institutions, ideas and structures were carried into the Constitution of India.
subconcepts: Government of India Act 1935 (provincial autonomy, federal scheme)
distinctions: Communal electorates (1909) vs separate electorates for Depressed Classes (1932)
foundation_focus: Learn the Acts as a timeline and what each added (e.g. codification, legislative council, dyarchy).
mains_focus: Trace which features of the 1935 Act reappear in the Constitution (federal scheme, emergency powers, Public Service Commissions, Governor's office).

subject: polity
title: Constituent Assembly and making of the Constitution
definition: The body formed under the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946) that framed the Constitution, adopted on 26 November 1949 and brought into force on 26 January 1950.
subconcepts: Composition and election of the Assembly
Role of the Drafting Committee and its chairman
Adoption vs commencement of different provisions
Debates on key issues (federalism, language, minority rights)
distinctions: Adoption date (26 Nov 1949) vs commencement (26 Jan 1950)
foundation_focus: Dates, key committees, Objectives Resolution and the Drafting Committee.
mains_focus: Link Assembly debates to design choices (strong Centre, language provisions, minority safeguards).

subject: polity
title: Preamble
definition: The introductory statement of the Constitution that declares its source (We, the People), the nature of the State and the objectives it secures.
subconcepts: Berubari Union case and Kesavananda Bharati on whether it is part of the Constitution
distinctions: Preamble as part of the Constitution vs enforceable source of power
Republic vs monarchy; secularism (Indian model) vs strict separation
foundation_focus: Word-by-word meaning, what the 42nd Amendment changed, judicial status.
mains_focus: Be able to use Preamble values (justice, liberty, equality, fraternity) as the frame for any governance answer.

subject: polity
title: Salient features and comparison with other constitutions
definition: The distinctive design choices of the Indian Constitution, many drawn from other constitutions and adapted to Indian conditions.
subconcepts: Features borrowed from the UK, US, Ireland, Canada, Australia, Weimar Germany, USSR, France, South Africa, Japan
distinctions: India vs UK (written vs unwritten, sovereignty)
foundation_focus: List the features and their sources accurately (high Prelims match-the-following value).
mains_focus: Compare India with one or two constitutions on a single feature and defend the Indian choice.

subject: polity
title: Union and its territory; citizenship
definition: Part I governs the Union and its territory (admission, formation, alteration of states); Part II governs who is a citizen and how citizenship is acquired and lost.
subconcepts: Articles 1–4 and Parliament's power to reorganise states
Reorganisation of states (States Reorganisation Act 1956; later states)
Citizenship Act 1955: birth, descent, registration, naturalisation, incorporation of territory
foundation_focus: Memorise the modes of acquiring/losing citizenship and the procedure under Art 3.
mains_focus: Be able to discuss citizenship law debates (e.g. CAA 2019) and state reorganisation as a federal question.

subject: polity
title: Fundamental Rights: definition of State and judicial review (Arts 12–13)
definition: Articles 12–13 define 'State' for Part III and make laws inconsistent with Fundamental Rights void, creating the basis for judicial review of legislation.
distinctions: Void ab initio vs void on inconsistency
foundation_focus: Understand who counts as 'State' and why it matters for enforcing rights.
mains_focus: Explain how Art 13 anchors judicial review and its interaction with Art 368.

subject: polity
title: Right to Equality (Arts 14–18)
definition: Guarantees equality before law and equal protection, prohibits discrimination, ensures equality of opportunity in public employment and abolishes untouchability and titles.
subconcepts: Art 14: equality before law, equal protection, reasonable classification
Art 16: equality in public employment; reservations; Indra Sawhney (creamy layer, 50% rule)
distinctions: Equality before law vs equal protection of laws
foundation_focus: Know each Article's text-level content, especially clauses added by amendments.
mains_focus: Argue formal vs substantive equality and reservation jurisprudence.

subject: polity
title: Right to Freedom (Arts 19–22) and Art 21
definition: Six freedoms under Art 19 (with reasonable restrictions), protection in respect of conviction (Art 20), life and personal liberty (Art 21), education (21A) and protection against arrest and detention (Art 22).
subconcepts: Art 19(1)(a)–(g) and grounds for restrictions under 19(2)–(6)
Art 20: ex post facto laws, double jeopardy, self-incrimination
Art 21: procedure established by law → due process (Maneka Gandhi)
Expanding content of Art 21 (privacy, dignity, health, environment)
distinctions: Procedure established by law vs due process
Absolute vs reasonable restrictions on freedoms
foundation_focus: Know the freedoms, restrictions and the major interpretations of Art 21.
mains_focus: Weigh liberty against public order, security and morality using case-law examples.

subject: polity
title: Rights against exploitation, to religion, and cultural-educational rights (Arts 23–30)
definition: Prohibits trafficking and forced labour, guarantees freedom of religion, and protects minority cultural and educational interests.
subconcepts: Art 24: child labour in hazardous work
Arts 25–28: freedom of conscience, practice and propagation; religious denominations; no compulsory taxes/instruction
Art 29: protection of minorities' language, script, culture
Art 30: minorities' right to establish and administer educational institutions
distinctions: Art 29 (any section of citizens) vs Art 30 (minorities)
foundation_focus: Know scope and limits of each Article.
mains_focus: Discuss secularism in India through freedom of religion and minority rights.

subject: polity
title: Right to Constitutional Remedies and writs (Arts 32, 226)
definition: The right to move the Supreme Court (Art 32) and High Courts (Art 226) for enforcement of rights, chiefly through the five writs.
subconcepts: Art 32 vs Art 226 (scope and territorial reach)
distinctions: Art 32 (a fundamental right itself) vs Art 226 (wider, non-fundamental-rights purposes too)
foundation_focus: Know each writ's purpose and when it is available.
mains_focus: Be able to explain why the right to remedies is called the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution and the role of PIL.

subject: polity
title: Directive Principles of State Policy
definition: Non-justiciable guidelines in Part IV directing the State to secure social and economic justice and build a welfare state.
distinctions: Fundamental Rights (justiciable, negative) vs DPSP (non-justiciable, positive)
Gandhian vs socialist vs liberal directives
foundation_focus: Group the directives by type and identify Articles.
mains_focus: Evaluate DPSPs as tools of welfare policy and how courts read them into rights.

subject: polity
title: Fundamental Duties
definition: Duties of citizens listed in Art 51A, added by the 42nd Amendment (1976) on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, with the eleventh added by the 86th Amendment (2002).
foundation_focus: List the duties and the amendments.
mains_focus: Discuss balance between rights and duties and whether duties should be enforceable.

subject: polity
title: Relationship between Fundamental Rights and DPSP
definition: The evolving judicial and legislative position on which prevails when rights and directives conflict, culminating in the 'harmony and balance' position.
subconcepts: Later judicial use of DPSP to expand Art 21
distinctions: Primacy of FR vs primacy of DPSP vs harmonious construction
foundation_focus: Know the cases and the sequence.
mains_focus: Explain how the Court moved from FR-primacy to a harmonious reading.

subject: polity
title: Amending the Constitution (Art 368)
definition: Art 368 prescribes how Parliament may amend the Constitution, with different majorities and, for some provisions, ratification by states.
subconcepts: Special majority (majority of the House plus two-thirds present and voting)
Special majority plus ratification by half of the states
distinctions: Amendment by simple majority (e.g. Art 3, 4) vs Art 368 amendment
foundation_focus: Memorise the three methods and examples of each.
mains_focus: Argue whether the amending procedure is balanced between flexibility and rigidity.

subject: polity
title: Basic structure doctrine
definition: Judicially evolved limit on Parliament's amending power: amendments cannot alter the basic structure or framework of the Constitution.
subconcepts: Indira Nehru Gandhi v Raj Narain (1975)
Waman Rao (1981): 24 April 1973 cut-off for Ninth Schedule
Illustrative features: supremacy, secularism, federalism, free and fair elections, judicial review, separation of powers
distinctions: Basic structure vs basic features (no exhaustive list)
Amending power vs ordinary legislative power
foundation_focus: Case sequence and the holding of each.
mains_focus: Argue the democratic legitimacy of judicial limits on constitutional amendment.

subject: polity
title: Landmark constitutional amendments
definition: Selected amendments that reshaped the polity, grouped by theme: rights and reservation, federal-fiscal, local government, electoral and parliamentary reform.
foundation_focus: Number–year–subject triplets for the amendments listed.
mains_focus: Group amendments by theme to support analytical answers on constitutional change.

subject: polity
title: Parliamentary system of government
definition: A system where the Executive emerges from, and is collectively responsible to, the legislature.
foundation_focus: Core features and examples of each.
mains_focus: Debate stability, accountability and the strengthening of the Prime Minister's office.

subject: polity
title: President of India
definition: Constitutional head of the Union Executive, elected indirectly, with executive, legislative, judicial, financial, diplomatic, military and emergency powers exercised on ministerial advice.
subconcepts: Discretion in hung Parliament; Art 74 and 42nd/44th Amendments
foundation_focus: Memorise the election method, term, removal and each power with its Article.
mains_focus: Be able to discuss the 'rubber stamp' debate and discretionary situations.

subject: polity
title: Vice-President of India
definition: Second-highest constitutional office; ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and acts as President during vacancy or absence.
distinctions: Vice-President's election vs President's election (electoral college composition)
mains_focus: Link to the role of presiding officers in legislative functioning.

subject: polity
title: Prime Minister and Council of Ministers
definition: The real executive: the PM heads a council collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha, with a Cabinet at its core.
subconcepts: Cabinet vs Council of Ministers vs Cabinet committees
Size limit (91st Amendment: 15% of Lok Sabha strength)
Ministers who are not members of Parliament (six months)
distinctions: Prime Minister vs President (real vs nominal)
mains_focus: Examine the 'primus inter pares' vs presidentialisation debate.

subject: polity
title: Parliament: composition, membership and disqualification
definition: Parliament consists of the President, the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha; its composition, qualifications and disqualification rules are constitutionally fixed.
subconcepts: Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha strength and term
distinctions: Lok Sabha (directly elected, dissolvable) vs Rajya Sabha (permanent house)
foundation_focus: Strength, term and mode of election of each House.
mains_focus: Evaluate bicameralism and the role of the Rajya Sabha in a federal polity.

subject: polity
title: Presiding officers of Parliament
definition: The Speaker, Deputy Speaker, Chairman and Deputy Chairman, who preside over and regulate proceedings of the Houses.
subconcepts: Powers: adjournment, casting vote, certifying Money Bill, deciding disqualification under Tenth Schedule
Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Vice-President) and Deputy Chairman
Neutrality and the 'Once a Speaker always a Speaker' convention
distinctions: Speaker vs Chairman of Rajya Sabha (election, removal)
mains_focus: Discuss the neutrality, anti-defection role and independence of the Speaker.

subject: polity
title: Legislative process: bills, Money Bills and joint sitting
definition: The passage of ordinary, money, financial and constitutional amendment bills, and the mechanisms to resolve deadlock between the Houses.
subconcepts: Ordinary bill: three readings, committee stage
Money Bill (Art 110) and Financial Bill categories
Role of Rajya Sabha on Money Bills
distinctions: Ordinary bill vs Constitution Amendment Bill
Government bill vs private member's bill
foundation_focus: Steps, categories and what each House can do.
mains_focus: Analyse efficacy of lawmaking: disruptions, scrutiny, delegated legislation, Money Bill route.

subject: polity
title: Budget and parliamentary financial control
definition: The constitutional framework by which Parliament authorises revenue and expenditure of the Union.
subconcepts: Consolidated Fund, Public Account, Contingency Fund
Appropriation Bill, Finance Bill, vote on account, supplementary grants
distinctions: Consolidated Fund vs Public Account vs Contingency Fund
foundation_focus: Funds, bills and stages in the budget cycle.
mains_focus: Assess Parliament's weak financial oversight and propose reforms.

subject: polity
title: Parliamentary committees
definition: Ad hoc and standing committees through which Parliament scrutinises the Executive and legislation.
foundation_focus: Composition and functions of each key committee.
mains_focus: Argue the case for referring more bills to committees.

subject: polity
title: Parliamentary devices and privileges
definition: Instruments (question hour, motions) used to hold the Executive to account, and the privileges that protect legislators and Houses.
subconcepts: Freedom of speech in the House
foundation_focus: Know each device and its purpose.
mains_focus: Discuss declining functioning of legislatures and measures to improve accountability.

subject: polity
title: Governor
definition: The constitutional head of a State, appointed by the President, with executive, legislative and limited discretionary powers.
subconcepts: Legislative powers incl. ordinances (Art 213) and reserving bills (Arts 200–201)
Sarkaria, Punchhi and other commission views
distinctions: Governor's discretion vs advice of the CoM
mains_focus: Evaluate the Governor's role in a federal system: appointments, floor tests, assent.

subject: polity
title: Chief Minister and State Council of Ministers
definition: The real executive of a State, collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.
subconcepts: CM's role with Governor and Council
distinctions: Chief Minister vs Prime Minister (parallel roles)
mains_focus: Link to state-level governance and coalition politics.

subject: polity
title: State Legislature
definition: The Legislative Assembly (and, in some states, the Legislative Council) with powers broadly parallel to Parliament within the State List and Concurrent List.
subconcepts: Legislative procedure and Money Bills in states
Comparison of Parliament and State Legislature
distinctions: Legislative Council vs Rajya Sabha (weaker role)
mains_focus: Evaluate whether second chambers in states are useful.

subject: polity
title: Federalism and Centre–State relations
definition: The distribution of legislative, administrative and financial powers between the Union and the States.
subconcepts: Seventh Schedule: Union, State, Concurrent Lists
Parliament's power to legislate on State List (Arts 249, 250, 252, 253)
distinctions: Legislative vs administrative vs financial relations
foundation_focus: Know the lists and the conditions under which Parliament can legislate on State subjects.
mains_focus: Evaluate recent flashpoints (GST, agriculture laws, Governor's role, central schemes).

subject: polity
title: Inter-State relations and coordination bodies
definition: Constitutional and statutory mechanisms for resolving inter-state disputes and coordinating policy.
subconcepts: Inter-State water disputes (Art 262; Inter-State River Water Disputes Act 1956)
Zonal Councils (statutory under the States Reorganisation Act 1956)
Public acts, records and judicial proceedings
NITI Aayog as a federal forum; GST Council
distinctions: Inter-State Council (constitutional provision, set up by President order) vs Zonal Councils (statutory)
foundation_focus: Bodies, Articles, how disputes are resolved.
mains_focus: Discuss river-water disputes and cooperative federalism.

subject: polity
title: Emergency provisions
definition: National Emergency (Art 352), President's Rule (Art 356) and Financial Emergency (Art 360) and their effects on federal and rights provisions.
subconcepts: Grounds and procedure for each emergency
Effect on Centre–State relations and Fundamental Rights (Arts 358–359)
distinctions: National vs State vs Financial Emergency
Art 358 (Art 19 suspended automatically) vs Art 359 (enforcement of rights suspended by order)
mains_focus: Evaluate S.R. Bommai and the misuse of Art 356.

subject: polity
title: Finance Commission and fiscal federalism
definition: The constitutional body that recommends sharing of Union taxes with the States and principles for grants-in-aid; part of the larger system of fiscal transfers including the GST Council.
subconcepts: Finance Commission vs Planning Commission/NITI Aayog
foundation_focus: Know the Articles and the roles of the bodies.
mains_focus: Analyse fiscal federalism issues: cesses and surcharges, GST compensation, devolution criteria.

subject: polity
title: Special provisions, Fifth/Sixth Schedules and Union Territories
definition: Asymmetric arrangements for particular states and regions: Art 370 (now abrogated), Art 371 series, tribal-area governance and the administration of Union Territories.
subconcepts: Fifth Schedule (Scheduled Areas) and Sixth Schedule (tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram)
foundation_focus: Know which state has which provision.
mains_focus: Assess asymmetric federalism and tribal self-governance.

subject: polity
title: Supreme Court of India
definition: The apex court with original, appellate, advisory and writ jurisdiction, custodian of the Constitution.
subconcepts: Court of record, review, curative petition
NJAC and the Fourth Judges case (2015)
distinctions: Original vs appellate vs advisory jurisdiction
mains_focus: Debate judicial appointments, pendency and the Court's role.

subject: polity
title: High Courts and subordinate courts
definition: The judicial hierarchy below the Supreme Court: High Courts with writ and supervisory powers, and district and subordinate courts.
subconcepts: Composition, appointment and removal of HC judges (Arts 214–217)
National Judicial Infrastructure and pendency issues
distinctions: High Court vs Supreme Court jurisdiction
mains_focus: Discuss pendency and judicial reform in lower courts.

subject: polity
title: Judicial review, judicial activism and PIL
definition: The power of courts to test laws and executive action against the Constitution, and its expansion through activism and public interest litigation.
subconcepts: Judicial activism vs judicial restraint vs overreach
PIL: origin, relaxation of locus standi
distinctions: Judicial review vs judicial activism vs judicial overreach
mains_focus: Argue merits and limits of judicial activism and PIL.

subject: polity
title: Separation of powers among organs
definition: How legislative, executive and judicial functions are distributed and checked in India, which follows functional overlap and checks rather than strict separation.
subconcepts: Overlaps: ministers in the legislature, delegated legislation, tribunals
Disputes between organs (e.g. legislative privilege vs judicial review)
distinctions: Separation of powers vs checks and balances
mains_focus: Evaluate conflicts between organs and ways to resolve them.

subject: polity
title: Tribunals and alternative dispute redressal
definition: Quasi-judicial and alternative mechanisms to reduce court load and provide specialised or quicker justice.
subconcepts: Lok Adalats and Legal Services Authorities Act 1987
National Green Tribunal and other statutory tribunals
mains_focus: Assess effectiveness and independence of tribunals and ADR.

subject: polity
title: Panchayati Raj (73rd Amendment)
definition: The constitutionally mandated three-tier system of rural local government under Part IX and the Eleventh Schedule.
subconcepts: Evolution: Balwant Rai Mehta, Ashok Mehta, L.M. Singhvi, Sarkaria
73rd Amendment: Gram Sabha, three-tier structure, direct elections, reservation, State Election Commission, State Finance Commission
Devolution of funds, functions and functionaries (3 Fs)
distinctions: PESA vs 73rd Amendment in Fifth Schedule areas
mains_focus: Evaluate why devolution to local bodies has lagged.

subject: polity
title: Urban local bodies (74th Amendment)
definition: The constitutional framework (Part IXA, Twelfth Schedule) for municipal governance in cities and towns.
subconcepts: Types of urban bodies: Municipal Corporation, Municipality, Notified Area Committee, Cantonment Board, Township etc.
distinctions: Elected vs bureaucratic control in cities
foundation_focus: Types of bodies and amendment provisions.
mains_focus: Discuss reforms in urban governance and finance.

subject: polity
title: Election Commission of India
definition: The constitutional body under Art 324 superintending, directing and controlling elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President.
subconcepts: Composition and appointment of the CEC and Election Commissioners
Registration and recognition of political parties and symbols
distinctions: Election Commission of India vs State Election Commission
mains_focus: Discuss independence of the Election Commission and electoral integrity.

subject: polity
title: Union and State Public Service Commissions
definition: Constitutional bodies (Part XIV) that recruit to civil services and advise on service matters, safeguarding merit-based recruitment.
mains_focus: Evaluate civil-service recruitment reforms.

subject: polity
title: CAG and law officers
definition: The Comptroller and Auditor General audits public accounts and the Attorney General is the Union's chief law officer.
mains_focus: Discuss CAG's independence and role in accountability.

subject: polity
title: National commissions for vulnerable sections
definition: Constitutional and statutory commissions protecting SCs, STs, backward classes, minorities, women and linguistic minorities.
mains_focus: Assess effectiveness of commissions as accountability mechanisms.

subject: polity
title: Statutory, regulatory and quasi-judicial bodies
definition: Bodies created by Acts of Parliament rather than the Constitution — human-rights, information, vigilance, anti-corruption and sectoral regulators.
subconcepts: Constitutional vs statutory vs executive bodies
foundation_focus: Parent Act, composition and role of each body.
mains_focus: Discuss effectiveness and independence of watchdog bodies.

subject: polity
title: Representation of the People Acts and the electoral system
definition: The statutes (RPA 1950, 1951) governing electoral rolls, conduct of elections, qualifications, disqualifications and disputes, and the first-past-the-post system used in India.
subconcepts: RPA 1950: delimitation, rolls, allocation of seats
RPA 1951: conduct, corrupt practices, disqualification (Sec 8), election petitions
Single transferable vote for RS/President elections
distinctions: Lok Sabha vs Rajya Sabha election methods
foundation_focus: What each Act covers and the electoral methods.
mains_focus: Compare electoral systems and argue for or against reform.

subject: polity
title: Electoral reforms
definition: Proposals and judicial/legislative changes to improve the fairness, transparency and inclusiveness of elections.
subconcepts: Committees (e.g. Dinesh Goswami, Tarkunde, Law Commission reports)
Right to know candidates' antecedents (ADR cases)
distinctions: Electoral reforms by court vs by legislature
foundation_focus: Know the major reforms and cases.
mains_focus: Argue pros and cons of specific reforms (simultaneous elections, state funding).

subject: polity
title: Anti-defection law (Tenth Schedule)
definition: The 52nd Amendment (1985) added the Tenth Schedule disqualifying legislators for defection; the 91st Amendment (2003) removed the one-third split exception.
subconcepts: Role of the Speaker/Chairman as decision-maker
distinctions: Speaker's role vs Election Commission's role (advice proposals)
mains_focus: Evaluate whether the Speaker should decide defection cases.

subject: polity
title: Political parties, party system and pressure groups
definition: How parties and organised interests function in the polity: recognition, funding, internal democracy, and the role of formal and informal associations.
subconcepts: National and state party recognition criteria
Pressure groups, interest groups and movements
mains_focus: Discuss the role of civil society and parties in a democracy.

subject: economy
title: Economic planning, 1991 reforms and NITI Aayog
definition: India's move from centrally directed Five-Year Plans to a market-oriented economy after 1991, and the replacement of the Planning Commission by NITI Aayog (2015).
subconcepts: Planned development: Five-Year Plans and their emphasis
Industrial licensing abolition and FERA to FEMA
Cooperative federalism role of NITI Aayog
distinctions: Planning Commission (allocative, Plan-based) vs NITI Aayog (think tank, no fund allocation)
foundation_focus: Know the sequence: plans, crisis, reforms, NITI Aayog.
mains_focus: Evaluate the effects of liberalisation on growth, industry and inequality.

subject: economy
title: National income and economic growth
definition: How the size and growth of an economy is measured (GDP, GNP, GVA and related aggregates) and the concepts needed to read growth data.
subconcepts: Gross value added vs GDP at market prices
Nominal vs real; base year; GDP deflator
mains_focus: Discuss sources of growth, jobless growth and inclusiveness.

subject: economy
title: Inflation and price indices
definition: Sustained rise in the general price level, how it is measured, and how policy responds.
subconcepts: Flexible inflation targeting and the Monetary Policy Committee
mains_focus: Evaluate monetary vs supply-side responses to food inflation.

subject: economy
title: Human development, poverty and employment
definition: Measures and policies concerning living standards, poverty, inequality, employment and social-sector schemes.
subconcepts: Poverty line and poverty estimation committees
Unemployment concepts: open, disguised, seasonal, structural
mains_focus: Critically assess welfare delivery and the link between growth and poverty reduction.

subject: economy
title: Money supply and monetary policy
definition: How the central bank influences money, credit and prices using policy rates and reserve requirements.
subconcepts: Repo, reverse repo, marginal standing facility, bank rate
Open market operations and liquidity adjustment facility
foundation_focus: Instruments and what each does to liquidity.
mains_focus: Assess the limits of monetary policy against supply-driven inflation.

subject: economy
title: Banking structure and the RBI
definition: The institutions of the banking system, the RBI's roles, and issues such as bad loans and resolution.
subconcepts: RBI functions: issuer, banker, regulator, FX manager
Scheduled commercial, regional rural, cooperative banks
distinctions: Payments bank vs small finance bank
foundation_focus: Types of banks and the RBI's functions.
mains_focus: Discuss NPA resolution, governance of public-sector banks and financial stability.

subject: economy
title: Financial markets and SEBI
definition: Markets for money, debt and equity, their instruments, and regulation.
subconcepts: Money market instruments (T-bills, commercial paper, certificates of deposit)
mains_focus: Assess the effect of foreign portfolio flows on stability.

subject: economy
title: Financial inclusion and digital payments
definition: Policies and technology that extend banking, credit, insurance and payment services to all.
subconcepts: Jan Dhan Yojana and direct benefit transfer
mains_focus: Evaluate gains and risks of digital finance for rural and vulnerable users.

subject: economy
title: Fiscal policy and the budget
definition: How the government raises and spends money, the deficit measures, and the legal framework for fiscal discipline.
subconcepts: Revenue vs capital receipts and expenditure
Fiscal, revenue, effective revenue and primary deficits
Outcome budget, zero-based budgeting, gender budgeting
distinctions: Fiscal deficit vs primary deficit vs revenue deficit
foundation_focus: Definitions and the formulas for each deficit.
mains_focus: Evaluate fiscal consolidation against growth and welfare needs.

subject: economy
title: Taxation and GST
definition: Types of taxes, the structure of Union and state taxation, and the Goods and Services Tax framework.
subconcepts: GST: CGST, SGST, IGST and UTGST
Black money, tax evasion vs avoidance
foundation_focus: Know the taxes and the GST design.
mains_focus: Assess GST outcomes and Centre-State fiscal tension.

subject: economy
title: External sector and balance of payments
definition: India's transactions with the rest of the world: BoP accounts, exchange rates, reserves and capital flows.
subconcepts: Current account deficit and its financing
Nominal vs real effective exchange rate
mains_focus: Analyse causes and risks of a widening current account deficit.

subject: economy
title: International trade and the WTO
definition: The rules and institutions of international trade and India's trade policy.
subconcepts: WTO agreements: GATT, GATS, TRIPS, AoA, TRIMS
Special economic zones and export promotion
Doha Round and agricultural subsidies disputes
Trade deficit and terms of trade
distinctions: Bilateral vs regional vs multilateral agreements
mains_focus: Discuss India's stand on agriculture subsidies and public stockholding at the WTO.

subject: economy
title: International economic institutions and reports
definition: Multilateral financial institutions and the major reports and indices they publish.
subconcepts: IMF: functions, quotas, special drawing rights
Asian Development Bank, AIIB, New Development Bank
Reports and indices that regularly appear in exams (published by which body)
foundation_focus: Which institution does what, and which report belongs to whom.
mains_focus: Discuss reform of global economic governance.

subject: economy
title: Agriculture, food security and rural development
definition: Cropping patterns, irrigation, support prices, subsidies, public distribution and land reforms.
subconcepts: Public Distribution System and National Food Security Act
Land reforms: zamindari abolition, tenancy, ceilings
distinctions: MSP vs procurement price vs issue price
mains_focus: Evaluate MSP, subsidies and market reforms in the context of farmer income and food security.

subject: economy
title: Industry and infrastructure
definition: Industrial policy, MSMEs and the infrastructure sectors that support growth.
subconcepts: Production-linked incentives and Make in India
Special economic zones and industrial corridors
distinctions: Public vs private vs PPP projects
mains_focus: Assess constraints on manufacturing growth and infrastructure financing.

subject: geography
title: Earth's interior, plate tectonics and landforms
definition: The structure and materials of the Earth and the processes that shape landforms.
distinctions: Convergent vs divergent vs transform boundaries
mains_focus: Explain a landform or hazard by linking it to plate tectonics.

subject: geography
title: Earth-Sun system, latitudes, longitudes and time
definition: Motions of the Earth, seasons, eclipses, coordinates and time zones.
subconcepts: Seasons and the inclination of the axis
Tides in relation to Sun and Moon
foundation_focus: Definitions and the causes of seasons and time differences.
mains_focus: Use geography reasoning for questions on day length, seasons and time.
keywords: revolution of the Earth|rotation of the Earth

subject: geography
title: Atmosphere and climatology
definition: Composition and structure of the atmosphere, heat balance, pressure, winds, cyclones and climate classification.
subconcepts: El Nino, La Nina and ENSO
distinctions: Convectional vs orographic vs cyclonic rainfall
mains_focus: Explain regional climates and extreme events with causes.

subject: geography
title: Oceanography
definition: Ocean relief, water properties, circulation, tides and marine resources.
subconcepts: Warm vs cold currents and climatic effects
mains_focus: Link currents to climate, fisheries and trade routes.

subject: geography
title: Physical features of India
definition: The Himalayas, northern plains, peninsular plateau, coastal plains, islands and desert.
subconcepts: Northern plains: bhabar, terai, bhangar, khadar
Peninsular plateau and Western and Eastern Ghats
Coastal plains of the west and east
